summary: Baures Airport (BVL) is a small airfield serving the remote town of Baures in the Beni Department of northeastern Bolivia. Located in the Amazonian lowlands near the Iténez River, it primarily handles light aircraft and occasional charter flights connecting this isolated riverside community to larger Bolivian cities. The airport plays a vital role in providing access to a region otherwise reachable mainly by river transport.
faqs:
Q: What type of aircraft typically uses Baures Airport?
A: The airport primarily handles small propeller aircraft and light charter planes suited to its short runway and remote location.

Q: Are there commercial scheduled flights to BVL?
A: Scheduled commercial service is limited or irregular; most flights are charter or on-demand operations serving the local community.

Q: What is the nearest major city to Baures Airport?
A: Trinidad, the capital of the Beni Department, is the closest major city and serves as a common connection point for travelers heading to Baures.

Q: Is the airport operational year-round?
A: Operations can be affected during the rainy season (roughly November to April) when flooding may impact the surrounding lowland area and runway conditions.
transport_tips: Travelers typically reach Baures Airport by connecting through Trinidad (TDD) and then taking a charter or small commercial flight. Ground transportation from the airport into Baures town is usually arranged locally, as formal taxi services are limited. River boats remain a popular alternative way to reach Baures from other parts of the Beni region.
local_tip: Carry cash in small Bolivian bills, as ATMs are uncommon in Baures and many local businesses, including those near the airport, may not accept cards.
